findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is null: mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration on undefined
findings.body: In EventManager.create(), `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields undefined when destinationCalendar is null/undefined, and the next line accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining (`evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`). The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which was null-safe. Any booking where destinationCalendar is null and location is Google Meet (e.g. handleNewBooking now explicitly sets destinationCalendar to null when neither eventType nor organizer has one) will throw a TypeError and abort booking creation.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent externalCalendarId fallback is dead code (find by externalCalendarId === null/undefined)
findings.body: In updateEvent: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — in the fallback branch externalCalendarId is falsy (null/undefined), so `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match, and selectedCalendar is undefined. The same broken pattern is repeated in deleteEvent (line 315-317). The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`; now update/delete are always sent with calendarId undefined, which for update sends an invalid request to the Google API and for delete silently falls back to "primary" (line 314/322), deleting from the wrong calendar when the event lives on a non-primary destination calendar.

findings.title: Organizer email forced to first host's destination calendar externalId even when event is created under a different host's credential
findings.body: In createEvent (and updateEvent), the organizer attendee's email is overridden with `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` — always the FIRST entry of destinationCalendar — regardless of which credential/selectedCalendar the event is actually created on. In a collective event with multiple hosts, when EventManager iterates the second host's destination calendar (different credentialId), the event is created on the second host's calendar but the organizer email still points at the first host's calendar externalId. This produces events attributed to the wrong organizer, can break Google Meet conference creation tied to the organizer, and causes mismatched organizer identity across hosts' calendars.

findings.title: createEvent silently falls back to "primary" when destinationCalendar has no entry for this credential
findings.body: `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` means that when destinationCalendar is non-empty but none of its entries has a matching credentialId (e.g. credential not in the list, or a stale destinationCalendar pointing at a removed credential), the event is silently created on the current credential's primary calendar instead of the intended destination. Combined with the 404-is-swallowed behavior in CalendarManager.createEvent, this can create duplicate/misplaced events on the wrong calendar with no error surfaced. It should log/skip when an explicit destination was requested but not found for this credential.

findings.title: Logic inversion: slug/requestedSlug conditions flipped from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED
findings.body: The diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`. Previously the slug was persisted on the team when team billing was disabled; now it is only set when billing is enabled. On instances without team billing, created organizations will no longer have a slug at all, breaking subdomain-based org URLs. This change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose and appears to be an accidental (or at least undocumented) behavior inversion; it should be reverted or justified.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent only honors the first destinationCalendar, so collective multi-host events are not created on other hosts' calendars
findings.body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent destructures only `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]` and filters calendars by that single externalId. Since EventManager now iterates all destinationCalendar entries and calls createEvent once per credential, a second host using a CalDAV-based calendar (Apple/iCloud/etc.) will have their event filtered out because their destination's externalId is never compared — only the first host's externalId is. The multi-host fix therefore does not work for CalDAV integrations; the filter should check whether any destinationCalendar entry matches the calendar, or the service should receive the specific destination being targeted.

findings.title: Only the first destinationCalendar is persisted on the booking row, losing other hosts' calendars for later operations
findings.body: When creating the booking record, the prisma connect uses `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` only. For collective events where evt.destinationCalendar contains multiple hosts' destination calendars, only the organizer's is connected to the Booking. Any code path that reconstructs the CalendarEvent from the booking without consulting references (e.g. requestReschedule, cancel fallbacks, reminders, payment webhooks) will therefore only see one destination calendar. The per-credential booking references partially compensate, but the persisted booking.destinationCalendar no longer reflects the event's full set of destination calendars.

findings.title: loadUsers rewrite changes error behavior and drops organization selection for dynamic bookings
findings.body: The rewritten loadUsers no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` for dynamic (non-eventType) bookings, so downstream code that relied on user.organization.slug for dynamic group bookings will now get undefined. Additionally, the new try/catch converts ordinary errors into a generic 500 "Unable to load users" and wraps Prisma known-request errors as 400s, changing the API error contract for dynamic bookings. These changes are incidental to the PR's purpose and untested.

findings.title: destinationCalendar payload shape changed from null/object to array — breaking change for webhook consumers
findings.body: The e2e snapshot updates show `destinationCalendar` in webhook payloads changing from `null` (or a single object) to `[]`/array of objects. This is an outward-facing breaking change to the BOOKING_* webhook payload contract that external integrations depend on; existing consumers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` or check `=== null` will break. The PR is labeled "non-breaking bug fix" but this is a public API contract change with no migration note or versioning.

findings.title: Recurring all-remaining cancellation deletes with the wrong credentials when references carry credentialIds
findings.body: In the allRemainingBookings branch inside the per-reference loop, deletion of updated bookings iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(type.endsWith("_calendar"))` rather than the reference's credentialId, and uses only the first calendar reference per updated booking (`updBooking.references.find(...)`). For collective events with multiple calendar references per booking (which this PR introduces), only the first reference's event is deleted per booking, leaving orphaned events on other hosts' calendars; and events may be deleted via the wrong credential, producing 404s.

findings.title: Fallback branch filters credentials by type === "calendar" but credential types are integration-specific (e.g. google_calendar)
findings.body: In createAllCalendarEvents' else branch (no destinationCalendar), the fallback filters `this.calendarCredentials.filter((cred) => cred.type === "calendar")`. No credential in the system has type exactly "calendar" (types are google_calendar, office365_calendar, etc.), so this fallback finds nothing and no calendar event is created at all. It should filter by type.endsWith("_calendar") (excluding other_calendar) or pick the first calendar credential, as the old code effectively did via destinationCalendar.

findings.title: No tests added for the multi-destinationCalendar collective booking behavior
findings.body: The PR checklist explicitly states no tests were added. The core change (destinationCalendar becoming an array, per-credential event creation for collective events, multi-reference update/cancel paths in EventManager and handleCancelBooking) is a substantial behavioral change affecting booking creation, reschedule, cancel, and payment webhooks, with several risky code paths (null destinationCalendar, fallback branches). At minimum, unit tests for EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents/updateAllCalendarEvents with multiple destinations and a null destinationCalendar case are needed before merging.
